storyworld_title: Reservoir Dogs: Blood on the Warehouse Floor

about_text.value: After the Karina Wholesale Diamonds heist explodes into a sidewalk slaughter, four color-coded survivors converge on an abandoned Los Angeles mortuary warehouse: protective veteran Mr. White, paranoid pragmatist Mr. Pink, smiling sadist Mr. Blonde with a kidnapped patrolman in his trunk, and gut-shot undercover detective Mr. Orange bleeding out on the ramp.

characters.name: Mr. White
characters.description: Lawrence Dimmick, an old-school heist professional whose protective loyalty toward bleeding Mr. Orange collides with cold evidence of an LAPD setup.

characters.name: Mr. Pink
characters.description: A hyper-rational career thief who stashed the Karina diamonds, refuses sentimental loyalty, and insists an informant tipped the police before the alarm sounded.

characters.name: Mr. Orange
characters.description: Freddy Newandyke, an undercover LAPD detective bleeding from a gut shot on the mortuary warehouse ramp while fighting shock, guilt, and blown cover.

characters.name: Mr. Blonde
characters.description: Vic Vega, a smiling ex-convict loyal to Joe Cabot who turned the diamond heist into a bloodbath and brought bound patrolman Marvin Nash in his trunk.

text_script.value: White drags Orange across the dusty mortuary floor. Blood soaks through the white dress shirt. Orange gasps, clutching White's sleeve. "Hospital. Real name. Please." Pink watches from the shadows, jaw tight. "No names. No hospitals. You're a liability, not a patient." White's hand finds Orange's pulse. "Hold the line, kid. We're not done." The shuttered room smells of cordite and stale coffee. Every breath tastes like copper. White's eyes flick to the steel door, then back to the bleeding detective. The crew's silence is a loaded gun.
Promise Orange help while enforcing color aliases

Orange's eyes flutter, a wet cough escaping his lips. "White... you're the only one who still talks like a man." Pink's thumb hovers over his phone, calculating odds. The promise hangs in the air, fragile as a bullet casing. Leverage shifts toward the ambush theory.

Orange nods weakly, the alias a shield against the pain. "Orange. Just Orange." White's grip tightens, a silent vow. Pink's eyes narrow, noting the discipline. The stash becomes the only safe harbor. Leverage shifts toward the color aliases and stash.

Orange's head lolls, a whisper of trust. "You'll get me out, White." Pink's jaw clenches, the math of betrayal already running. The promise is a thread, and the ambush is the knife. Leverage shifts toward the ambush theory.
Whisper your first name to steady the dying kid

Orange's eyes widen, a flicker of humanity breaking through the shock. "Freddy... just Freddy." White's voice drops to a murmur, the name a secret. Pink's expression hardens, the alias rule shattered. Leverage shifts toward the color aliases and stash.

Orange's breath shudders, the name a lifeline. "Freddy... hold on." White's hand stays on the pulse, the name a ghost. Pink's eyes track the shift, the ambush theory gaining traction. Leverage shifts toward the ambush theory.

Orange's lips move, the name a prayer. "Freddy... don't let them take me." White's grip tightens, the alias a fragile shield. Pink's jaw sets, the stash the only refuge. Leverage shifts toward the color aliases and stash.
Search Orange's coat and pockets for tail transmitters

Orange's eyes roll back, a groan escaping his throat. "White... what are you doing?" White's fingers dig into the coat, the search a violation. Pink's eyes narrow, the ambush theory confirmed. Leverage shifts toward the ambush theory.

Orange's hand twitches, a silent plea. "Please... just the name." White's search pauses, the alias a bargaining chip. Pink's eyes track the hesitation, the stash the only safe ground. Leverage shifts toward the color aliases and stash.

Orange's breath hitches, the search a betrayal. "You're not... you're not a cop, are you?" White's fingers find nothing, the ambush theory a shadow. Pink's jaw tightens, the math of suspicion. Leverage shifts toward the ambush theory.
Lock the steel rollup door and stage the getaway car

Orange's eyes track the door, a flicker of hope. "White... the car?" White's hand on the wheel, the alias a shield. Pink's eyes narrow, the stash the only refuge. Leverage shifts toward the color aliases and stash.

Orange's head lolls, the door a promise. "White... don't leave me." White's grip on the wheel tightens, the ambush theory a shadow. Pink's eyes track the shift, the math of betrayal. Leverage shifts toward the ambush theory.

Orange's breath shudders, the car a lifeline. "White... just the name." White's hand on the wheel, the alias a fragile shield. Pink's jaw sets, the stash the only safe ground. Leverage shifts toward the color aliases and stash.

Pink slams the side door, winded, satchel clutched tight. "SWAT was already in position before Blonde pulled a trigger. I ran the math. The alarm tripped before his first shot." Orange coughs blood onto the concrete. Blonde leans against a morgue drawer, grinning. "Maybe the math's wrong, Pink. Maybe the rat's closer than you think." Pink's eyes narrow. "I don't care who's bleeding. I need that satchel location. Now."
Pink, recount the exact timeline of the Karina vault ambush

Pink's jaw tightens. He lists timestamps with cold precision, each second a weapon. Orange's breathing hitches, but his eyes stay locked on the satchel. The room holds its breath, waiting for the next accusation to land.
Blonde chuckles, a wet, rattling sound. He shifts his weight, testing the door. "Timeline's a hell of a thing to remember when you're bleeding out, Pink. Maybe the cops just got lucky."
Pink's gaze snaps to the satchel. "Lucky? No. Someone called it in. And I know who. The math doesn't lie, and it points to a color in this room."
Blonde, your panic shooting explains the whole bloody mess
Blonde's smile falters, just for a second. He wipes blood from his lip. "Panic? I don't panic. I adapt. You want to blame me, Pink? Fine. But you're still holding that satchel."
Pink steps closer, voice dropping to a dangerous whisper. "You brought a cop in your trunk, Blonde. That's not panic. That's a setup. And I'm not done counting the bodies."
Blonde's eyes narrow. He reaches for his gun, but his hand trembles. "You're right. I brought a cop. But I also brought the diamonds. And I'm not giving them up. Not yet."
Where did you hide the diamond satchel, Pink?
Pink's hand tightens on the satchel. "You think I'd hide it where you can find it? No. It's in a place only I know. And if you want it, you're going to have to bleed for it."
Blonde laughs, a broken, painful sound. "You're hiding it? Pink, you're the one who ran. You're the one who's scared. And you're the one who's lying."
Pink's eyes flick to Orange. "You're bleeding, Freddy. You're dying. And you're still here. That means you're not a cop. That means you're one of us. And I need you to tell me where the satchel is."

Cigarette smoke curls over the bathroom sink. Mr. Orange moans from the wooden ramp, blood pooling beneath his gut. Mr. Pink stares at the floor, calculating. "Stones are stashed. Minutes away. If we move, we die. If we stay, we bleed out." Mr. White grips a pistol, eyes locked on the door. "Who knew the vault schedule?" The shuttered mortuary smells of cordite and stale coffee. Every breath tastes of betrayal. The crew weighs discipline against the certainty that an LAPD plant sold them out.
Hold the safehouse until Joe Cabot and Nice Guy Eddie call.
Mr. Blonde’s grin tightens as he hears the engine outside. He checks his gun, eyes flicking to the door. "They’re here. Let’s see if the cops brought friends or just more blood."
Mr. Pink’s jaw clenches. He glances at the Cadillac trunk, knowing what’s inside. "If they’re in that trunk, we’re done. I’m not dying for a cop’s mistake."
Mr. White’s hand trembles slightly. He looks at Orange, then at the door. "If they’re here, we’re not alone. We need to move now, before the whole crew turns on us."
Offer Pink control of the satchel in exchange for a doctor.
Mr. Pink’s eyes narrow. He steps closer to the satchel, fingers brushing the leather. "A doctor? You think I’m buying a doctor with my diamonds? I’m buying survival."
Mr. Blonde laughs, a low, dangerous sound. "A doctor? You’re offering a cop a doctor? That’s not a deal, that’s a suicide note."
Mr. White’s voice is steady, but his eyes are cold. "If you want the satchel, you want the doctor. No exceptions. No sentiment."
Cross-check who knew the Karina vault schedule in advance.
Mr. Blonde’s smile fades. He looks at Pink, then at White. "You’re saying one of us is a rat? That’s not a question, that’s an accusation."
Mr. Pink’s voice is flat, but his eyes are sharp. "I’m saying the vault schedule was known. Someone leaked it. And I’m not the one who did it."
Mr. White’s hand tightens on his gun. He looks at Orange, then at the door. "If we don’t find the rat, we’re all dead. And I’m not dying for a cop’s mistake."

Mr. Blonde leans against the support beam, slurping a striped drive-thru cup. Mr. White and Mr. Pink shout over Mr. Brown's cracked skull and dead Mr. Blue. White lunges at him for slaughtering civilians. Blonde's hand drifts toward his shoulder holster. Every breath inside the shuttered mortuary smells of cordite, stale coffee, and drying arterial blood, forcing each survivor to weigh professional discipline against the creeping certainty that an LAPD plant sold out the crew.
Step between White and Blonde with cold syndicate discipline.
Blonde's smile tightens, his thumb resting on the holster. White's eyes narrow, reading the shift in leverage. The tension snaps taut, pushing the group toward the Cadillac trunk.
Blonde's eyes flick to the chair, calculating the next move. White's hand hovers near his weapon. The standoff shifts, forcing a pivot toward the chair and duct tape.
Blonde's grip on the cup tightens, a subtle threat. White's discipline holds, but the air thickens. The group's focus shifts back to the Cadillac trunk, a looming consequence.
Pin Blonde against the pillar and strip his backup piece.
Blonde's eyes flash with cold fury. White's hand moves to the chair, a tactical pivot. The leverage shifts, forcing a move toward the chair and duct tape.
Blonde's hand twitches, a silent warning. White's grip tightens on the pillar. The tension escalates, pushing the group toward the Cadillac trunk.
Blonde's smile vanishes, replaced by a cold stare. White's eyes narrow, reading the shift. The standoff resolves toward the chair and duct tape.
Watch Orange's eyes while Blonde recounts the alarm trip.
Blonde's voice drops, a low, precise recount. White's eyes track Orange's reaction. The tension shifts, pushing the group toward the Cadillac trunk.
Blonde's eyes flick to the chair, a subtle threat. White's hand hovers near his weapon. The standoff shifts, forcing a pivot toward the chair and duct tape.
Blonde's grip on the cup tightens, a silent threat. White's discipline holds, but the air thickens. The group's focus shifts back to the Cadillac trunk.

Blonde pops the Cadillac trunk. Marvin Nash blinks up from the spare-tire well, duct tape sealing his mouth. Sirens wail in the alley. White steps forward, face grim. "Drag him inside. Demand answers." Pink stares at the cop's badge. "You brought a beacon to our safehouse, you idiot." Blonde smiles, blood on his teeth. "Maybe the beacon's already ringing, Pink."
Drag the cop inside, White, and demand answers about the patrol

White yanks Nash by the collar, dragging him into the mortuary's shadow. Pink watches, calculating the risk. The cop's eyes dart, seeking an escape route. White's voice drops to a lethal whisper, "Talk, or I make you talk."

Nash struggles, his cuffs clinking. Pink steps back, hand near his gun. "You're making a mistake, White. He's a cop. He's a beacon." White ignores him, focusing on Nash's face, searching for the truth behind the uniform.
Blonde leans against the Cadillac, grinning. "See? He's alive. He's a cop. He's a beacon. And we're all screwed." White's jaw tightens. He drags Nash deeper into the shadows, away from the sirens.
Blonde, you brought a live cop beacon to our safehouse, you idiot
Blonde's smile falters. "Beacon? I brought a cop, Pink. He's a cop. He's a beacon. He's a cop." Pink's eyes narrow. "You're a cop, Blonde. You're a beacon. You're a cop."
White steps between Pink and Blonde. "Stop it. Both of you. We need answers, not accusations." Nash's eyes widen. He sees the tension. He sees the danger. He sees the end.
Pink pulls out his phone. "I'm calling Eddie. I'm calling Eddie. I'm calling Eddie." Blonde's smile returns. "Eddie's a cop. Eddie's a beacon. Eddie's a cop." White's hand tightens on his gun.
Check Nash's service radio frequency before touching the tape, Pink
Pink kneels, examining Nash's radio. "Frequency 15.1. That's the patrol channel. He's broadcasting. He's a beacon. He's a cop." White's face hardens. "Then we silence him. Now."
Blonde laughs. "Silence him? He's a cop. He's a beacon. He's a cop." Pink stands, radio in hand. "I'm calling Eddie. I'm calling Eddie. I'm calling Eddie." White's hand tightens on his gun.
Nash's eyes dart. He sees the radio. He sees the danger. He sees the end. White steps forward. "Talk, or I make you talk." Nash's lips move, but no sound comes out. The sirens grow louder.

Duct tape bites into Marvin Nash's wrists. Mr. Orange bleeds silently on the warehouse floor, his eyes fixed on the ceiling. Mr. Pink leans close, voice clipped. "Who called the stakeout?" Mr. Blonde grins, cracking his knuckles. "I want to hear him scream first." Mr. White watches the blood pool, calculating the odds. The air smells of cordite and stale coffee. Every second stretches. Pink wants methodical answers. Blonde wants pain. Orange wants to die. The warehouse holds its breath, waiting for the next move.
Ask Nash about precinct stakeout orders and possible moles

Nash's jaw tightens, a bead of sweat tracing his temple. He glances at Pink, then away, his voice trembling. "You don't know what you're dealing with, Pink. The stakeout was clean. Someone inside the precinct fed you the diamonds. I'm just the messenger."

Blonde snorts, stepping closer to Nash. "Clean? You're bleeding out, cop. And your boss just called the cops. Pink, let me have him. I'll get the truth out of him before he drops. Pink, you're just watching."

White's eyes narrow, his hand drifting toward his hip. He watches Nash's micro-expressions, the slight flinch when Pink mentions the diamonds. "You're lying, Nash. The stakeout wasn't clean. Someone in this room sold us out. Pink, you know it."
Let Blonde rough Nash up while Pink watches for tells

Blonde grabs Nash's collar, yanking him forward. "Talk, cop. Who called?" Nash's eyes widen, his breath hitching. Pink watches, his face unreadable, but his fingers drum against his thigh. "He's stalling. Blonde, keep him talking. I need to know if the mole is still in the precinct."
Nash's head snaps back, a wet cough escaping his lips. "Please, I'm not the one who called. I'm just a patrolman. The stakeout was set by someone else. Pink, you're wrong. The mole is in this room."
Blonde releases Nash, stepping back with a satisfied grin. "He's got something to say. Pink, you're right. The mole is in this room. And I'm going to find out who. White, you're next."
Pull Pink aside to compare Orange's commode story cadence

White steps between Pink and the chair, his voice low. "Pink, come here. We need to talk. Orange's story about the commode, the way he described it, it's off. Too detailed. Too rehearsed. He's lying."
Pink follows White, his eyes narrowing. "You think Orange is the mole? He's bleeding out, White. He's not going anywhere. And his story? It's consistent. He's not lying."
White's jaw tightens. "Consistent? That's what a mole would do. Pink, you're too close to this. You're not seeing it. Orange's story is a setup. He's feeding us false information."

The phone buzzes on the blood-slicked floor. Eddie's voice cuts through the cordite haze. "Where's the satchel?" Pink wipes his hands. "In the trunk. You want it?" Orange coughs, a wet rattle. "He's not coming back." White grips the receiver. "Eddie, listen. The diamonds are gone. We're done." The line clicks dead. Pink stares at the dead phone. "He's not coming back," Orange repeats, his eyes rolling. "He's not coming back," White whispers, the words tasting like ash.
Grab Pink, secure diamonds, and warn Blonde to stop torturing

Pink snarls, grabbing the satchel. "You're dead, White. I'm taking the diamonds and the car. You can stay with the rat." His eyes lock on Orange, who slumps, blood pooling. The leverage shifts to Pink's escape, leaving White and Orange to face the consequences of the betrayal.

Orange's eyes snap open, blood dripping from his lip. "He's not coming back," he rasps, his hand twitching toward the gun. White freezes, the weight of the receiver heavy. The tension spikes, Orange's pain sharpening his focus, and the threat of his gun becomes the immediate consequence, forcing a standoff.

White's jaw tightens, his grip on the phone slipping. "Eddie's not coming back," he says, the words a confession. Pink laughs, a dry, hollow sound. "Good. We're done here." The silence stretches, the phone dead, and the consequence is the finality of the crew's dissolution, leaving them to face the aftermath.
Hide a micro-check in Blonde's gasoline can and keys

Orange's eyes widen, blood spattering the floor. "He's not coming back," he whispers, his hand trembling. White's hand moves to the gasoline can, his fingers brushing the keys. The tension is palpable, the weight of the secret heavy. The consequence is the immediate threat of Orange's gun, forcing a quick decision.

Pink's eyes narrow, his gaze fixed on White's hand. "You're not hiding anything," he says, his voice low. White's hand stops, the keys clinking. The silence is thick, the weight of the secret pressing down. The consequence is the shift in leverage, Pink's suspicion growing, and the threat of his gun becoming real.

Orange's eyes roll back, his body going limp. White's hand freezes, the keys clinking. The silence is absolute, the weight of the secret heavy. The consequence is the finality of Orange's death, leaving White and Pink to face the aftermath, the phone dead, the crew dissolved.
Press Orange on why Mr. Blue vanished during the alley split

Orange's eyes snap open, blood dripping from his lip. "He's not coming back," he rasps, his hand twitching toward the gun. White's voice is low, pressing. "Where's Blue?" Orange's eyes narrow, the pain sharpening his focus. The consequence is the immediate threat of his gun, forcing a standoff.

Pink's eyes narrow, his gaze fixed on Orange. "You're not going to answer that," he says, his voice low. Orange's eyes roll back, his body going limp. The silence is thick, the weight of the secret pressing down. The consequence is the shift in leverage, Pink's suspicion growing, and the threat of his gun becoming real.

The silence stretches, the phone dead, and the consequence is the finality of the crew's dissolution, leaving them to face the aftermath.

Gasoline slicks the concrete as Marvin Nash sobs, his uniform soaked. "I got a kid at home, I swear!" Mr. Blonde thumbs a chrome Zippo, the flame licking the damp air. Mr. Orange raises a trembling Smith & Wesson from the ramp, his gut wound pulsing. The shuttered mortuary reeks of cordite and stale coffee. Every breath tastes of betrayal. Orange’s finger hovers near the trigger, weighing professional discipline against the creeping certainty that an LAPD plant sold out the crew. The lighter clicks. The gun shakes. The silence stretches, thin as a razor, waiting for the next move.
Empty the cylinder into Blonde's chest before the Zippo drops.

Blonde’s head snaps back, eyes wide with shock. The Zippo clatters to the floor, flame dying. Nash screams, pointing at the body. Orange’s hand shakes, blood dripping from his wound. The warehouse falls silent, the smell of gunpowder mixing with gasoline. The crew’s loyalty fractures, replaced by the cold reality of a dead witness and a compromised mission.

Blonde’s body twitches, his last breath a whisper. Nash cowers, backing into the shadows. Orange’s face hardens, guilt and rage warring. The Zippo’s flame flickers out. The warehouse echoes with the sound of a dying man and the wet drip of blood. The crew’s plan collapses, leaving only the hollow truth of a job gone wrong.

Nash's eyes dart to the shuttered door. The smell of stale coffee and drying blood fills the room. Every breath is a negotiation. The crew weighs professional discipline against the creeping certainty that an LAPD plant sold them out. The silence stretches, thick and dangerous.
Swear Nash to silence and rehearse the Blonde-betrayal cover story

Nash nods, his jaw tight. White grips his shoulder, a silent promise of protection. Pink watches, calculating the risk. The leverage shifts toward the Blonde story, but the fear of Cabot's wrath lingers, pulling the crew toward a darker verdict.

Nash's eyes flicker with doubt. White's grip tightens, a subtle threat. Pink smirks, sensing weakness. The crew's focus narrows to Cabot's potential arrival, the silence breaking as the threat of the verdict looms larger than the Blonde story.

Joe fires at Orange, White shoots Joe, Eddie shoots White, and White drops Eddie in a deafening three-second thunderclap. Crawling across the blood-slick floor to cradle Freddy's head, Larry hears the whispered truth—'I'm a cop'—and presses his barrel under Orange's chin as police boots burst open the warehouse door in a hail of rifle fire.

While ego and blood oaths detonate the center of the warehouse, Mr. Pink stays crouched beneath the wooden ramp with both hands locked around the Karina diamond satchel. Slipping into the sun-bleached alley seconds before SWAT rams the front rollup, the only man who treated the heist like a job vanishes into the sirens with two million in uncut stones.

Unchecked sadism turns the safehouse into an inferno as spilled gasoline catches a stray muzzle flash under the tinny groove of seventies AM radio. Black smoke pours from the mortuary vents before Joe Cabot's sedan even clears the corner, drawing every patrol unit in East Los Angeles onto ashes, melted tape, and ruined alibis.

Convinced by the timeline gaps and Pink's cold ambush arithmetic, Mr. White lowers his forty-five half an inch when Joe Cabot calls Freddy Newandyke a plant. Joe finishes the job without blinking, tosses Pink the car keys, and scatters the surviving crew through freight yards two minutes ahead of the robbery-homicide encirclement.

Refusing to watch the kid bleed out on concrete for Joe Cabot's rules, Larry Dimmick abandons the diamond split and shoulders Freddy into a stolen sedan bound for emergency surgery. Under harsh triage fluorescents, detectives greet Mr. White with drawn service weapons while Freddy grips his sleeve from the gurney, saved by the thief he was sent to cage.

encounters.title: Secret Ending: The Commode Tell and the Culvert Exit

text_script.value: Catching the rehearsed squad-room cadence in Orange's anecdote without letting Blonde's razor blow the room apart, White and Pink force a quiet confession before Joe Cabot ever reaches the block. Leaving Marvin Nash alive beside Freddy with a ninety-second ambulance call, Larry and Pink slip down the dry storm culvert with the Karina satchel—no massacre, no cuffs, and one haunted debt paid in full.
